patterns.note: The hero section uses a large, off-center headline with a subtle, blurred central image, creating a spacious and modern focal point.
Feature sections (e.g., AI Fashion Photoshoot) are presented with a primary, large visual on the left and a grid of related smaller images on the right, demonstrating variety.
The 'How it Works' section employs a full-width, vertically stacked design with large, numbered steps that visually progress down the page.
Two-column grid layouts with a prominent text block on one side and an image/content placeholder on the other are used for showcasing product benefits (e.g., 'Your product', 'Campaign-ready').
Major headlines frequently use two contrasting font styles or colors for emphasis, combining a vibrant accent (orange) with a muted tone (gray) to highlight key words.
The 'How it Works' summary (e.g., 'Stays on-brand Create Images Makes videos') uses varying font sizes, weights, and opacities to indicate an active state versus inactive or upcoming actions.
Large, bold sans-serif typography dominates headings, creating a strong, contemporary, and easily scannable visual hierarchy.
A vibrant orange serves as the primary accent color, consistently used for calls to action, active states, and to draw attention to key textual elements.
The 'How it Works' section utilizes a sequence of distinct, full-width gradient backgrounds (e.g., orange, blue, purple, red) to visually differentiate each step of the process.
A predominantly neutral palette of white, off-white, and various shades of gray provides a clean, expansive backdrop, allowing vibrant accent colors and product imagery to stand out.
The 'How it Works' section implies scroll-triggered background transitions and text emphasis, where each step becomes visually prominent as it enters the viewport.
Dedicated feature showcase sections (e.g., 'AI Fashion Photoshoot', 'AI Product Shots') use visual galleries and brief descriptions to demonstrate specific capabilities of the service.
A 'How it Works' section breaks down the product's usage into a clear, numbered, step-by-step workflow, guiding the user through the process.

technique_notes: To create split heading emphasis, use separate inline elements within a heading tag, applying different colors and font weights (e.g., a vibrant color for one word, a muted gray for another) to each part.

Implement scroll-linked section background changes by using JavaScript (e.g., an Intersection Observer) to detect when a new section enters the viewport, then update a global CSS variable or apply a class to trigger a background color or gradient transition on a main content wrapper.

Design interactive feature carousels by arranging multiple image cards in a grid that allows for horizontal scrolling or discrete navigation, often with an active state highlighted for the currently viewed content.
